label: Settlement chronology
quiz: Which sequence correctly compares the colonial developments?
Cebu: 1565 Spanish settlement; Manila: 1571 Spanish city
Manila: 1571 before Cebu: 1565
Both places began all local history in 1571
Both developments happened during Magellan's 1521 voyage
retry: What does the 1571 date for Manila describe in this lesson?
Establishment of the Spanish city within a place with earlier history
The first time any person lived in the region
The creation of every trading link in Asia
Immediate effective control of all Philippine islands
hard: A museum label says Cebu began in 1565. What is the strongest correction?
Specify the Spanish settlement, while acknowledging the earlier community
Move all local history to Manila in 1571
Remove the date and claim the place had no earlier residents
Say the date proves every resident agreed

label: Existing communities
quiz: What evidence helps challenge the idea that Maynila was empty before the Spanish city?
The earlier polity associated with Rajah Sulayman
Only the date of the later colonial council
Only an outsider's drawing of empty land
The claim that colonial offices created all people
retry: Why should an exhibit name Tupas and Sulayman in their own settings?
To recognize earlier leadership without treating one person as everyone
To show that the names belong to one person
To prove all residents shared one opinion
To replace evidence with a familiar name
hard: A label says Spanish offices introduced every kind of leadership. What does it overlook?
Existing local leaders and organized communities
Only the colour of arriving ships
Only the later spelling of a place name
The need to make both dates identical

label: Trade and place
quiz: Which explanation best connects a port with trade?
A landing place works with merchants, supplies and regional connections
A useful location guarantees every transaction succeeds
Every network began with Spanish newcomers
A port makes local decisions irrelevant
retry: How did regional merchants matter to the Spanish presence?
They helped connect newcomers with existing trade centered in Luzon
They had no role because geography alone traded goods
They created all Philippine communities from nothing
Their participation proved consent to every colonial demand
hard: A diagram shows a port beside a community. What further evidence would explain exchange?
Who moved and supplied goods and how connections were maintained
Only a larger arrow on the same diagram
Only a claim that trade never required people
Only the assumption that profit was guaranteed

label: Different local responses
quiz: Which statement fits the Bangkusay evidence used in this mission?
Some communities resisted the Spanish presence in 1571
Every nearby community accepted colonial rule without opposition
The marker names every participant's private motive
One event shows the same choice by all communities
retry: Why is one Cebu agreement insufficient to describe every Manila Bay community's choice?
The agreement had particular participants and did not decide for everyone elsewhere
All communities had exactly the same leadership
An agreement removes the need to study resistance
Nearby places always share one opinion
hard: A caption attaches Rajah Sulayman's name to the Macabebe leader in the marker without evidence. What should a learner do?
Keep the identity stated by the source and avoid substituting a familiar name
Use the familiar name because all leaders are interchangeable
Invent a speech to confirm the name
Ignore the source and copy the caption

label: Institutions and reach
quiz: What is an institution in this lesson?
An organized body with continuing duties, such as a city council
Only a ship passing the shore
A guarantee that every island obeys
The exact feelings of all local people
retry: Why does a written order not establish authority everywhere?
Its actual enforcement and local responses still need evidence
Writing the order makes every person agree automatically
All places were one household
An institution eliminates all practical limits
hard: A report shows a council issued an order but claims control of all islands. What evidence is missing?
Where the order was carried out, with what resources and responses
Only the council's name written a second time
Only a larger drawing of the town
Only the date of an earlier voyage
